suggestions.rationale: Neurologic symptoms radiating into the legs are a recognized associated finding with chronic lumbar spine conditions. VA guidance directs that associated objective neurologic abnormalities be evaluated separately.
evidenceGaps: Exam or imaging documenting radiculopathy and the affected nerve
Identification of which extremity or extremities are involved
Severity characterization (mild, moderate, or severe incomplete paralysis)

sourceReferences.note: General Rating Formula for Diseases and Injuries of the Spine, Note (1), addressing separate evaluation of associated objective neurologic abnormalities.
Schedule of ratings, neurological conditions, including the sciatic nerve.

suggestions.rationale: Frequently assessed where radiating leg pain is documented. Overlaps substantially with radiculopathy; the two should not be claimed in a way that double-counts the same impairment.
evidenceGaps: Clinical findings distinguishing sciatica from other sources of leg pain
Documentation of which nerve distribution is involved
Review for overlap with any radiculopathy claim

sourceReferences.note: Schedule of ratings, neurological conditions, sciatic nerve.

suggestions.rationale: Sustained chronic pain is sometimes linked to depressive symptoms. Requires a diagnosis from a qualified mental health provider and an opinion addressing the pain relationship.
evidenceGaps: Mental health diagnosis from a qualified provider
Documentation of pain chronicity and functional impact
Nexus opinion addressing chronic pain as the cause or aggravating factor
